newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish authorities turn back fleeing villagers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish authorities turn back fleeing villagers.

text.p: Turkish provincial authorities, struggling with a population boom, on Thursday sent hundreds of Kurdish villagers fleeing a guerrilla conflict back to their homes, Anatolian news agency said.
It said local officials refused to let 270 villagers from the southeastern province of Hakkari settle in the neighbouring province of Van.
"Forty-five families from the village of Doganli in Hakkari...who wanted to settle in Van were sent back," the agency said. "They were taken out of Van this morning on buses."
Hakkari, on the mountainous border with Iraq, is scene of some of the heaviest fighting in a 12-year-old conflict between troops and Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas.
Residents of Hakkari, one of Turkey's poorest areas, have flooded into Van in recent years.

The Hurriyet daily quoted local official Hasan Kayhan as saying Van could take no more fleeing villagers. "Our population has increased to 600,000 from 153,000 due to the immigrants. We do not want any more trouble," he said.
Human rights workers say troops have forcibly evacuated around 3,000 villages in the conflict, mostly in the 1990s.
But Turkey blames the rebels for emptying the settlements and says accusations that its forces evacuate villages are an attempt by guerrilla supporters to smear it.
"We do not even have bread to eat. We do not want to leave our place but the villages around us were emptied," Hurriyet quoted an unnamed villager as saying.
More than 26,000 people have died since the fighting began in 1984, when the PKK took up arms for Kurdish self rule.
